page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and includes 150 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core operations and memory bandwidth. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU physics and extended instructions tests. Large-block memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 695.05 GB/sec for read-only and 347.3 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance remains strong, placing in the top 25% for Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, though single-threaded compression and static web serving throughput fall into the middle 50% average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the hpc7a.24xlarge offers high memory-to-core ratios and dedicated compute resources, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive parallel processing without hyperthreading overhead. However, the complete absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The lack of GPU acceleration also limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it demonstrates strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference.

This configuration is suited for high-performance computing workloads, large-scale scientific simulations, multi-threaded software compilation, and memory-intensive database operations. It is also highly capable for Redis in-memory data store operations, where it achieves top-tier throughput.
